_: Single owner of how an agent reaches a model. Read by Nix (modules/gateway.nix) and by Guile (guix/home-configuration.scm). Rationale and vocabulary: CONTEXT.md; seam decision: docs/adr/0001-gateway-facts-cross-the-guix-seam-as-json.md. Nothing here is a secret -- only the name of one.
_models: Addressing's other half: which ids exist, and the ceilings a harness must respect to hold them. Was duplicated across pi's models.json on M-02877 and Caveman Code's on mahakala, and the two disagreed (home-manager-8vh). Slot names are roles a harness asks for; ids are what the gateway publishes. contextWindow and maxTokens are the gateway's own enforced ceilings, measured 2026-09-19: it names its limit in the 400 body, both for max_tokens ('N > M, which is the maximum allowed number of output tokens') and for an oversized prompt ('prompt is too long: N tokens > M maximum'). GET /v1/models is not served (404), so a probe is the only first-hand source; re-measure rather than edit from memory.

haiku._reasoning: Stays false: a configured thinking level on Haiku 4.5 trips 'adaptive thinking is not supported on this model' (LEGO/ai-model-gateway-client, src/features/docs/pages/PiPage.tsx).
haiku.name: Haiku 4.5 (LEGO)

headroom._noMemoryTools: Headroom 0.40.0 answers its injected memory_save/memory_search tools server-side; when the model also called a client tool in the same turn, the continuation leaves that call unanswered and the provider rejects it with a 400 mid-stream (headroomlabs-ai/headroom#4009, fix in #4013). This stops the injection only: memory storage and --learn stay on. Drop it once a release has #4013.
headroom._excludeTools: Headroom 0.40.0 lossy-compresses caveman_retrieve output, so the original Caveman recovers arrives rewritten (headroomlabs-ai/headroom#4010, fix in #4014). Excluded tools still get lossless cleanup, so indented JSON arrives minified. Drop it once a release has #4014.
headroom._allowUnauthenticatedBind: Headroom images from 2026-10 refuse to bind 0.0.0.0 unless HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN is set, because their /v1/* routes would relay the caller's gateway credential to anyone who can reach the port. A token does not fit here: local-model-proxy and the harnesses already send the gateway key as the Authorization bearer, so a second bearer would collide with it. The image's documented alternative is this acknowledgement. It is honest only while every host publishes the port on loopback (published.*.host); on the container network, only our own sibling containers can reach it. Measured 2026-10-06: without it headroom exits at start, and local-model-proxy then loops on 'could not resolve headroom container IP'.
